page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-8-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the c3 server family. It features 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, configured with a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The underlying hardware is powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. This configuration provides 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, yielding 2 threads per core. The processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It is equipped with 804 GB of local NVMe SSD storage across two physical drives, but does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results place the c3-standard-8-lssd in the average performance tier for most standard operations. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests yield scores of 1622.99 and 6655.81 respectively, while Geekbench scores reach 1702.0 for single-core and 6546.0 for multi-core tasks. Memory bandwidth is measured at 544.39 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 55.2 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 33.89 GB/sec for large-block writes. The server demonstrates average capabilities in database operations, processing 8.89 million Redis SET operations per second, and achieves a static web serving throughput of 13.23 GB/sec.

While the server performs adequately across general workloads, certain performance tradeoffs exist. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is relatively weak, scoring 35.19 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Similarly, while prompt processing for a 7B LLM model reaches 51.34 tokens/sec, text generation on the same model is limited to 7.69 tokens/sec. The inclusion of 804 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside dedicated CPU resources offers balanced resource density for workloads requiring fast local scratch space. This server is configured for general-purpose computing, software compilation, web serving, and database operations that benefit from local NVMe storage.
